content.content:
29	## 1. The Business
30	
31	You are building part of the rent collection module of a property management platform used by Malaysian property management companies.
32	
33	- Each organization (a property management company) rents units to tenants under leases.
34	- A lease produces invoices: an optional deposit, plus one rent invoice per monthly period.
35	- Tenants pay by cash, by bank transfer (with an uploaded slip), or online through a payment gateway. Payments are allocated to invoices.
36	- Business timezone: Asia/Kuala_Lumpur (UTC+8, no daylight saving). Currency: MYR (RM). 1 ringgit = 100 sen.
37	- Your server runs in UTC and our assessors work from several timezones. Every date and time the app shows or accepts is Malaysia time, whatever the timezone of the server or of the viewer's device.
38	
39	### Roles
40	
41	| Role    | Who                | Can                                                                                                                                    |
42	| ------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
43	| manager | Organization admin | Everything in their organization: create leases, record payments (approved immediately), approve, reject and void payments, read the audit log |
44	| staff   | Front desk         | Read their organization's leases, invoices and payments; record payments (these wait for a manager's approval)                         |
45	| tenant  | Renter             | Read their own profile, leases, invoices and payments; update their own phone number; pay online                                       |
46	
47	A staff member or manager belongs to exactly one organization. Nobody ever sees another organization's data.
48	
49	## 2. Local Setup and Seed Data
50	
51	Develop against a local Supabase stack (Docker and the Supabase CLI), not a cloud project. See Supabase local development. We grade by running your project on our machine from a fresh clone, with exactly these commands:
52	
53	```bash
54	npx supabase start            # starts the stack from your supabase/config.toml
55	npx supabase db reset         # rebuilds the database from supabase/migrations/
56	npm install
57	cp .env.example .env.local    # we replace keys with the values from `npx supabase status` if they differ
58	npm run seed
59	npm run build && npm start
60	```
61	
62	Commit supabase/config.toml, supabase/migrations/, and an .env.example that lists every variable your app needs, with local values and a comment saying where each one comes from.
63	
64	npm run seed creates exactly the data below on a freshly reset database, through your normal code paths (your lease creation and payment logic), so the invoices and allocations it produces are the ones your app would produce.
65	
66	All seeded accounts share one password of your choice, which you submit with your work.
67	
68	### Organizations and accounts
69	
70	| Organization         | Account                | Role    | Notes                                                                        |
71	| -------------------- | ---------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
72	| Northwind Properties | manager@northwind.test | manager |                                                                              |
73	| Northwind Properties | staff@northwind.test   | staff   |                                                                              |
74	| Northwind Properties | aisyah@northwind.test  | tenant  | Tenant "Aisyah Rahman"                                                       |
75	| Northwind Properties | ben@northwind.test     | tenant  | Tenant "Ben Lim"                                                             |
76	| Northwind Properties | probe@northwind.test   | tenant  | Tenant "Probe Tenant" (our tests create payments and leases for this tenant) |
77	| Beta Realty          | manager@beta.test      | manager |                                                                              |
78	| Beta Realty          | chen@beta.test         | tenant  | Tenant "Chen Wei"                                                            |
79	
80	### Units and leases
81	
82	| Organization | Unit   | Tenant        | Start      | End        | Monthly rent | Deposit     |
83	| ------------ | ------ | ------------- | ---------- | ---------- | ------------ | ----------- |
84	| Northwind    | A-12-3 | Aisyah Rahman | 2026-01-31 | 2026-07-15 | RM 1,500.00  | RM 3,000.00 |
85	| Northwind    | B-05-1 | Ben Lim       | 2026-01-01 | 2026-04-15 | RM 1,000.29  | none        |
86	| Northwind    | C-01-7 | Probe Tenant  | 2026-02-28 | 2027-02-27 | RM 2,000.00  | RM 4,000.00 |
87	| Northwind    | D-03-2 | (no lease)    |            |            |              |             |
88	| Beta         | KL-1   | Chen Wei      | 2026-03-15 | 2027-03-14 | RM 2,200.00  | RM 4,400.00 |
89	
90	### Payments on Aisyah's lease
91	
92	- Cash, RM 3,000.00, received 2026-01-31 10:00 Malaysia time, recorded by the manager.
93	- Bank transfer, RM 2,000.00, received 2026-03-01 00:30 Malaysia time, recorded by staff with a slip file, then approved by the manager.
94	
95	## 3. Billing Rules - lib/billing.ts
96	
97	Create lib/billing.ts (or src/lib/billing.ts). It must be pure: no I/O, no imports from Next.js, React, Supabase or Prisma, and no dependence on the timezone of the machine it runs on. Your app must use it, and we test it directly.
98	
99	```ts
100	export type InvoiceKind = 'deposit' | 'rent'
101	
102	export interface ScheduledInvoice {
103	  kind: InvoiceKind
104	  periodIndex: number | null  // 0, 1, 2... for rent; null for the deposit
105	  periodStart: string | null  // 'YYYY-MM-DD'; null for the deposit
106	  periodEnd: string | null    // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive; null for the deposit
107	  dueDate: string             // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
108	  amountSen: number           // integer
109	}
110	
111	export function generateSchedule(lease: {
112	  startDate: string           // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
113	  endDate: string             // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive (the tenant's last day)
114	  monthlyRentSen: number
115	  depositSen: number
116	}): ScheduledInvoice[]
117	
118	export type InvoiceStatus = 'paid' | 'partially_paid' | 'unpaid' | 'overdue'
119	
120	export function invoiceStatus(
121	  invoice: { dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number },
122	  now: Date,
123	): InvoiceStatus
124	
125	export function parseRinggitToSen(input: string): number
126	```
127	
128	### generateSchedule
129	
130	- Validation. Throw an Error if a date is not a real calendar date written as YYYY-MM-DD, if endDate is before startDate, if monthlyRentSen is not a positive integer, or if depositSen is not a non-negative integer.
131	- Deposit. If depositSen > 0, the first invoice is the deposit: kind: 'deposit', due on startDate, period fields null.
132	- Anchors. Rent periods are anchored on the start date. The anchor of period k is the start date plus k calendar months, always counted from the start date (never from the previous anchor). If that month has fewer days than the start day, use the month's last day. A lease starting on Jan 31 has anchors Jan 31, Feb 28 (Feb 29 in leap years), Mar 31, Apr 30, and so on.
133	- Periods. Period k runs from anchor k to the day before anchor k+1, and is due on anchor k. There is a period for every anchor on or before endDate.
134	- Last period. It is cut at endDate. If it is shorter than its full length, it costs monthlyRentSen x days used / days in the full period, rounded half up to the nearest sen. Every other period costs monthlyRentSen.
135	- Order. The deposit first, then rent by period index.
136	
137	Worked example (Aisyah's lease):
138	
139	| Period  | Kind | Dates                    | Due        | Amount      |
140	| ------- | ---- | ------------------------ | ---------- | ----------- |
141	| deposit |      |                          | 2026-01-31 | RM 3,000.00 |
142	| 0       | rent | 2026-01-31 to 2026-02-27 | 2026-01-31 | RM 1,500.00 |
143	| 1       | rent | 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-30 | 2026-02-28 | RM 1,500.00 |
144	| 2       | rent | 2026-03-31 to 2026-04-29 | 2026-03-31 | RM 1,500.00 |
145	| 3       | rent | 2026-04-30 to 2026-05-30 | 2026-04-30 | RM 1,500.00 |
146	| 4       | rent | 2026-05-31 to 2026-06-29 | 2026-05-31 | RM 1,500.00 |
147	| 5       | rent | 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-15 | 2026-06-30 | RM 774.19   |
148	
149	Period 5 uses 16 of the 31 days from 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-30: 150000 x 16 / 31 = 77419.35, so 77419 sen.
150	
151	### invoiceStatus
152	
153	Apply these rules in order:
154	
155	1. paid if paidSen >= amountSen.
156	2. overdue if today's Malaysia date is after dueDate. An invoice due 2026-03-01 becomes overdue at 2026-03-02 00:00 Malaysia time (2026-03-01T16:00:00Z), not a moment earlier.
157	3. partially_paid if paidSen > 0.
158	4. Otherwise unpaid.
159	
160	### parseRinggitToSen
161	
162	Turns what a user types into sen. It accepts digits with optional comma thousands separators (groups of exactly three digits) and an optional decimal part of one or two digits, ignoring whitespace around the value: "1,500.50" gives 150050, "1.15" gives 115, "7" gives 700. Anything else throws an Error, for example "", "-5", "1.234", "1e3", "RM 10", "1,23".
163	
164	## 4. Payments
165	
166	### Recording a payment
167	
168	- Staff and managers record cash or bank transfer payments on a lease: the amount, the method, and the date and time the money was received (entered and shown in Malaysia time).
169	- A bank transfer needs a slip: a JPEG, PNG or PDF of at most 5 MB, stored in Supabase Storage (section 6). If recording fails after the upload, the file must not be left behind.
170	- A payment recorded by a manager is approved immediately. A payment recorded by staff is pending_verification until a manager approves or rejects it.
171	- Cap. A new payment may not be more than the lease's remaining balance (the total of all its invoices minus everything allocated to them) minus the total of the lease's payments still pending_verification. Paying future periods in advance is allowed within the cap.
172	
173	### Approving, rejecting and voiding (managers only)
174	
175	- Approve a pending_verification payment. At that moment, check again that it is not more than the lease's remaining balance. If it is, refuse and leave it pending.
176	- Reject a pending_verification payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters.
177	- Void an approved payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters. Voiding removes that payment's allocations. Other payments' allocations do not change.
178	- Payments are never deleted. Every approval, rejection, void and lease creation writes a row to audit_log (who, what, when, details).
179	
180	### Allocation
181	
182	When a payment becomes approved, its amount is allocated to the lease's invoices that still have something unpaid, in this order: due date, then deposit before rent, then period index. Each invoice is filled up to its unpaid amount before the next one, including invoices that are not due yet. Whatever is left once every invoice is fully paid is stored on the payment as unapplied_sen. Only online payments can end up with an unapplied amount, because manual payments are capped.
183	
184	The paid amount of an invoice is the sum of its allocations. Statuses are computed with invoiceStatus, never stored.
185	
186	All of this must stay correct when requests arrive at the same time. For example, two staff members recording payments on the same lease at once must not exceed the cap together, and a payment approved twice at once is allocated once.
187	
188	### Collections report
189	
190	The total of approved payments for each calendar month of received_at in Malaysia time, over a range of months, including months with nothing collected. With the seed data, Northwind's report for 2026-01 to 2026-03 is [{ month: '2026-01', collectedSen: 300000 }, { month: '2026-02', collectedSen: 0 }, { month: '2026-03', collectedSen: 200000 }].
191	
192	## 5. Online Payments
193	
194	A tenant pays online like this:
195	
196	1. The tenant clicks Pay now on their lease. Your API creates a gateway bill for the amount due now: the unpaid amounts of the lease's invoices due on or before today's Malaysia date. If nothing is due, refuse. Bill ids must be impossible to guess.
197	2. In production the tenant would now be redirected to the gateway. In this test, show the bill id and amount: we play the gateway using the simulator below.
198	3. The gateway calls your webhook, POST /api/webhooks/gateway. Only the webhook can settle a bill. The gateway also sends the tenant back to /payments/return?bill_id=...&paid=true. That page only shows the bill's real status from your database and changes nothing.
199	
200	### Webhook
201	
202	The request body is application/x-www-form-urlencoded, with these fields. The gateway may add more fields in future.
203	
204	| Field              | Example                    | Notes                                                    |
205	| ------------------ | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
206	| id                 | bill_8f3a2c                | Your bill id (this short example is guessable; yours must not be) |
207	| paid               | true                       | true or false                                            |
208	| paid_amount        | 210050                     | Amount in sen; 0 when not paid                           |
209	| paid_at            | 2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800  | When it was paid                                         |
210	| transaction_id     | TX-000123                  | Gateway transaction id                                   |
211	| transaction_status | completed                  | completed, failed or pending                             |
212	| x_signature        | 06994f...                  | See below                                                |
213	
214	Signature. Take every field in the request except x_signature, sort them by key (ascending by character code), write each one as the key immediately followed by the value, join them with |, and compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the resulting string with your secret key GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY, as lowercase hex. Test vector, with the key test_x_signature_key and the six example values above:
215	
216	```text
217	source:    idbill_8f3a2c|paidtrue|paid_amount210050|paid_at2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800|transaction_idTX-000123|transaction_statuscompleted
218	signature: 06994fab2d674e7829144eaa2204631716d3c099b503d38945e92b6296531641
219	```
220	
221	Required behavior:
222	
223	| Situation                                           | Response | Effect                                                                                               |
224	| --------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
225	| Signature missing or wrong                          | 401      | None                                                                                                 |
226	| Unknown bill id                                     | 404      | None                                                                                                 |
227	| paid=true and paid_amount is not the bill's amount  | 422      | None                                                                                                 |
228	| paid=true, bill pending or failed                   | 200      | Bill becomes paid, and one approved online payment is created with received_at = paid_at, then allocated |
229	| paid=true, bill already paid (a repeat delivery)    | 200      | None                                                                                                 |
230	| paid=false, bill pending                            | 200      | Bill becomes failed                                                                                  |
231	| paid=false, bill already failed (a repeat delivery) | 200      | None                                                                                                 |
232	| paid=false, bill already paid (late or out of order)| 200      | None: a paid bill never goes back                                                                    |
233	
234	The gateway retries, so it may deliver the same callback several times, including at the same moment. A bill creates at most one payment, ever. Never log the secret key or whole callback payloads.
235	
236	### Simulator
237	
238	Save this as gateway-sim.mjs and run node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> [true|false] with GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY set.
239	
240	```js
241	import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'
242	
243	const [billId, amountSen, paid = 'true'] = process.argv.slice(2)
244	const url = process.env.WEBHOOK_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/gateway'
245	const key = process.env.GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY
246	
247	const myt = new Date(Date.now() + 8 * 3600 * 1000).toISOString()
248	const fields = {
249	  id: billId,
250	  paid,
251	  paid_amount: paid === 'true' ? amountSen : '0',
252	  paid_at: `${myt.slice(0, 10)} ${myt.slice(11, 19)} +0800`,
253	  transaction_id: `TX-${Date.now()}`,
254	  transaction_status: paid === 'true' ? 'completed' : 'failed',
255	}
256	const source = Object.keys(fields).sort().map(k => `${k}${fields[k]}`).join('|')
257	fields.x_signature = createHmac('sha256', key).update(source).digest('hex')
258	
259	const res = await fetch(url, {
260	  method: 'POST',
261	  headers: { 'content-type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
262	  body: new URLSearchParams(fields),
263	})
264	console.log(res.status, await res.text())
265	```
266	
267	## 6. Access Control
268	
269	Access is enforced in two places, and we test both:
270	
271	1. Your server code: route handlers, Server Actions and server components. Every endpoint must authenticate the caller and check their organization and role itself. A protected page or a hidden button is not a check.
272	2. The Supabase Data API and Storage, which anyone holding your publishable key can call directly with their own access token.
273	
274	### Server code
275	
276	- Roles come from your memberships table, and from tenants.user_id for tenants. Never take a role or an organization from anything the user can edit, such as user_metadata.
277	- On the server, authenticate with supabase.auth.getUser() or getClaims(), not getSession().
278	- A request about a record in another organization, or another tenant's record, gets 404: do not reveal that it exists. A request about a record the caller can see, for an action their role does not allow, gets 403. A request without a valid login gets 401.
279	- IDs in request bodies are untrusted too. For example, a manager must not be able to create a lease on another organization's unit or tenant.
280	- Our tests call your API with Authorization: Bearer <access token>, where the token is a Supabase access token for one of the seeded users. Accept that header as well as the normal session cookie.
281	- The service role (secret) key must never reach the browser.
282	
283	### Data API
284	
285	This table is the most access allowed through the Supabase Data API, which is PostgREST called with a user's token. Granting less is fine where your app does not need it, with one exception: the tenant portal reads the tenant's own data, and updates their phone number, directly from the browser with supabase-js.
286	
287	| Table                                                       | anon | tenant                            | staff                 | manager               |
288	| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---- | --------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------- |
289	| organizations                                               | none | read own organization             | read own organization | read own organization |
290	| memberships                                                 | none | none                              | read own organization | read own organization |
291	| units                                                       | none | read the units of own leases      | read own organization | read own organization |
292	| tenants                                                     | none | read own row, update only phone   | read own organization | read own organization |
293	| leases, invoices, payments, payment_allocations, gateway_bills | none | read the rows of own leases    | read own organization | read own organization |
294	| audit_log                                                   | none | none                              | none                  | read own organization |
295	
296	Every other insert, update or delete through the Data API must fail for everyone. This covers every table, view and function (/rest/v1/rpc/...) you create, not just the ones above. audit_log is append-only for every role, including the service role and the database owner.
297	
298	### Storage
299	
300	Bank transfer slips go in a private bucket named payment-slips, under <org_id>/.... Only staff and managers of that organization can upload there, and they read slips through short-lived signed URLs. Tenants, other organizations and anonymous users cannot read, list or upload slips. A payment's slip_path must point to an existing file in its own organization's folder.
301	
302	## 7. HTTP API
303	
304	Request and response bodies are JSON, except for the webhook. Amounts are integers in sen. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and instants are ISO 8601 with an offset. Errors return { "error": "message" }.
305	
306	| Method and path                                      | Who                                | Success                                             | Other responses                                         |
307	| ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
308	| POST /api/leases                                     | manager                            | 201 { id }                                          | 400 invalid input, 409 overlaps another lease on the unit |
309	| GET /api/leases/:leaseId                             | staff, manager, the lease's tenant | 200, shape below                                    |                                                         |
310	| POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments                   | staff, manager                     | 201 { id, status }                                  | 400 invalid input, 422 over the cap                     |
311	| POST /api/payments/:paymentId/approve                | manager                            | 200 { status }                                      | 409 not pending, 422 over the remaining balance         |
312	| POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject                 | manager                            | 200 { status }                                      | 400 missing reason, 409 not pending                     |
313	| POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void                   | manager                            | 200 { status }                                      | 400 missing reason, 409 not approved                    |
314	| POST /api/leases/:leaseId/gateway-bills              | the lease's tenant                 | 201 { billId, amountSen }                           | 422 nothing due                                         |
315	| GET /api/reports/collections?from=YYYY-MM&to=YYYY-MM | staff, manager                     | 200 [{ month: 'YYYY-MM', collectedSen }], one entry per month in order | 400 invalid range                    |
316	| POST /api/webhooks/gateway                           | the gateway                        | see section 5                                       |                                                         |
317	
318	Every endpoint also returns 401, 403 and 404 as described in section 6. Request bodies:
319	
320	```ts
321	// POST /api/leases
322	{ unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
323	
324	// POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments
325	{ amountSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer'; receivedAt: string; slipPath?: string }
326	
327	// POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject and POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void
328	{ reason: string }
329	```
330	
331	GET /api/leases/:leaseId returns the invoices in allocation order:
332	
333	```ts
334	{
335	  lease: { id: string; unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
336	  invoices: {
337	    id: string; kind: 'deposit' | 'rent'; periodIndex: number | null; periodStart: string | null; periodEnd: string | null
338	    dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number; status: InvoiceStatus
339	  }[]
340	  payments: {
341	    id: string; amountSen: number; unappliedSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer' | 'online'
342	    status: 'pending_verification' | 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'voided'; receivedAt: string
343	  }[]
344	}
345	```
346	
347	Creating a lease stores the lease and exactly the invoices generateSchedule returns, all or nothing. Leases on the same unit never overlap (both dates are inclusive), even when two requests arrive at the same moment.
348	
349	## 8. Database
350	
351	Keep every database object in SQL migrations under supabase/migrations/: tables, constraints, RLS policies, grants, functions, triggers, and the storage bucket and its policies. npx supabase db reset must rebuild all of it; nothing may depend on changes made by hand in Supabase Studio. Use Prisma for server-side data access, with prisma/schema.prisma matching the database.
352	
353	Store money as integer sen (bigint), never as a floating-point type. Calendar dates are date, and instants are timestamptz.
354	
355	Required tables and columns (add whatever else you need):
356	
357	| Table               | Required columns                                                                                     |
358	| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
359	| organizations       | id, name                                                                                             |
360	| memberships         | user_id, org_id, role (manager or staff)                                                             |
361	| units               | id, org_id, name                                                                                     |
362	| tenants             | id, org_id, user_id, full_name, email, phone                                                         |
363	| leases              | id, org_id, unit_id, tenant_id, start_date, end_date, monthly_rent_sen, deposit_sen                  |
364	| invoices            | id, org_id, lease_id, kind, period_index, period_start, period_end, due_date, amount_sen             |
365	| payments            | id, org_id, lease_id, amount_sen, unapplied_sen, method, status, received_at, slip_path, gateway_bill_id |
366	| payment_allocations | id, org_id, payment_id, invoice_id, amount_sen                                                       |
367	| gateway_bills       | id, org_id, lease_id, amount_sen, status (pending, paid or failed)                                   |
368	| audit_log           | id, org_id, actor_id, action, entity_id, details, created_at                                         |

content.content:
-- =============================================================================
-- 1/4 Schema: tables, constraints, indexes. RLS is enabled here, on every table,
-- in the same migration that creates it; the policies themselves are in
-- 20261020100622_access_control.sql (no policy = no row is visible, so every
-- table is closed from the moment it exists).
--
-- Conventions
--   * money        : bigint, integer sen, columns named *_sen (never float/numeric)
--   * calendar day : date (lease start/end, billing periods, due dates)
--   * instant      : timestamptz (received_at, paid_at, created_at)
--   * every table carries org_id; child tables reference their parent through a
--     composite FK (parent_id, org_id) -> parent(id, org_id), so a row can never
--     point at a parent in another organization, whatever the app sends.
--   * user_id columns hold auth.users.id but have no FK: Prisma introspection
--     refuses cross-schema FKs unless the whole auth schema is pulled into the
--     client. A trigger (integrity_triggers.sql) checks the user exists instead.
-- =============================================================================

-- btree_gist lets a GiST exclusion constraint compare uuids with "=", which the
-- "no two leases on one unit overlap" constraint needs. Installed in the
-- `extensions` schema: functions in `public` would be callable as /rest/v1/rpc.
create extension if not exists btree_gist with schema extensions;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Privileges. Supabase's default privileges grant anon/authenticated ALL on
-- every new table, sequence and function in `public`. Undo that before creating
-- anything; access_control.sql then grants back only what the brief allows.
-- (ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES affects objects created by the current role,
-- postgres, which is the role that runs these migrations.)
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
alter default privileges in schema public revoke all on tables from anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges in schema public revoke all on sequences from anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges in schema public revoke all on functions from public, anon, authenticated;

-- All our functions (RLS helpers, trigger functions) live in `private`, a schema
-- PostgREST does not expose, so no /rest/v1/rpc/... endpoint exists for them.
create schema if not exists private;
-- Functions get EXECUTE for PUBLIC by default; in `private` nothing is callable
-- unless granted explicitly.
alter default privileges in schema private revoke execute on functions from public;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- organizations: a property management company. The tenancy boundary.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.organizations (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name       text not null check (char_length(btrim(name)) > 0),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
alter table public.organizations enable row level security;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- memberships: staff and managers. unique (user_id) = a staff member or manager
-- belongs to exactly one organization (the brief's rule, enforced by the DB).
-- Roles come from here, never from user_metadata.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.memberships (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id    uuid not null unique,  -- auth.users.id (no FK: see note at top)
  org_id     uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  role       text not null check (role in ('manager', 'staff')),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index memberships_org_id_idx on public.memberships (org_id);
alter table public.memberships enable row level security;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- units
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.units (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id     uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  name       text not null check (char_length(btrim(name)) > 0),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (org_id, name),
  -- Target of the composite FK from leases. id is first so this index also
  -- serves plain lookups by id (it is the selective column).
  unique (id, org_id)
);
alter table public.units enable row level security;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- tenants: a renter, scoped to one organization. user_id links the auth account
-- (nullable: a tenant record can exist before it has a login). unique (user_id)
-- means one login is one tenant row, so a tenant also sees exactly one org.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.tenants (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id     uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  user_id    uuid unique,           -- auth.users.id (no FK: see note at top)
  full_name  text not null check (char_length(btrim(full_name)) > 0),
  email      text not null check (position('@' in email) > 1),
  -- Tenants edit this themselves through the Data API, so the format is checked
  -- here, not only in the UI: optional +, then digits, spaces or dashes.
  phone      text check (phone ~ '^\+?[0-9][0-9 -]{6,19}$'),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index tenants_org_id_idx on public.tenants (org_id);
alter table public.tenants enable row level security;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- leases. Both dates are inclusive (end_date is the tenant's last day).
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.leases (
  id               uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id           uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  unit_id          uuid not null,
  tenant_id        uuid not null,
  start_date       date not null,
  end_date         date not null,
  monthly_rent_sen bigint not null check (monthly_rent_sen > 0),
  deposit_sen      bigint not null check (deposit_sen >= 0),
  -- auth user who created it. Deliberately no FK: it is a historical fact that
  -- must survive the user being deleted (same for recorded_by, decided_by...).
  created_by       uuid,
  created_at       timestamptz not null default now(),
  check (end_date >= start_date),
  -- The unit and the tenant must belong to the lease's own organization.
  foreign key (unit_id, org_id) references public.units (id, org_id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, org_id) references public.tenants (id, org_id),
  unique (id, org_id),
  -- No two leases on the same unit overlap. '[]' = both bounds inclusive.
  -- An exclusion constraint is checked by the index itself, so two concurrent
  -- inserts cannot both succeed (the second waits, then fails with 23P01) —
  -- a "select overlapping then insert" check in the app could not promise that.
  constraint leases_no_overlap exclude using gist (
    unit_id with =,
    daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') with &&
  )
);
create index leases_org_id_idx on public.leases (org_id);
create index leases_unit_id_org_id_idx on public.leases (unit_id, org_id);
create index leases_tenant_id_org_id_idx on public.leases (tenant_id, org_id);
alter table public.leases enable row level security;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- invoices: exactly what lib/billing.ts generateSchedule returns for the lease.
-- No status column: status is computed by invoiceStatus(), never stored.
-- No paid column: paid = sum(payment_allocations.amount_sen), never stored.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.invoices (
  id           uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id       uuid not null,
  lease_id     uuid not null,
  kind         text not null check (kind in ('deposit', 'rent')),
  period_index integer,
  period_start date,
  period_end   date,          -- inclusive
  due_date     date not null,
  -- >= 0, not > 0: a prorated last period of one day can round to 0 sen.
  amount_sen   bigint not null check (amount_sen >= 0),
  created_at   timestamptz not null default now(),
  constraint invoices_period_shape check (
    (kind = 'deposit' and period_index is null and period_start is null and period_end is null)
    or
    (kind = 'rent' and period_index >= 0 and period_start is not null
      and period_end >= period_start and due_date = period_start)
  ),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases (id, org_id),
  unique (id, org_id),
  -- One rent invoice per period AND at most one deposit per lease: the deposit
  -- is the row whose period_index is NULL, and NULLS NOT DISTINCT makes a
  -- second NULL for the same lease a duplicate. (A partial unique index
  -- `where kind = 'deposit'` would say the same, but Prisma introspects it as
  -- lease_id being unique and generates a wrong one-to-one relation.)
  constraint invoices_lease_id_period_index_key
    unique nulls not distinct (lease_id, period_index)
);
-- Allocation order: due date, then deposit before rent, then period index.
-- (Deposit rows have period_index NULL; ASC puts NULLs last, so the query must
-- order by (kind = 'deposit') desc explicitly — the index just narrows to lease.)
-- lease_id leads, so this index also covers the (lease_id, org_id) FK.
create index invoices_allocation_order_idx
  on public.invoices (lease_id, due_date, period_index);
create index invoices_org_id_idx on public.invoices (org_id);
alter table public.invoices enable row level security;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- gateway_bills: an online payment request. The id is what the gateway echoes
-- back and what the tenant sees, so it must be unguessable: 'bill_' + 128 bits
-- of gen_random_uuid() randomness (122 random bits) as 32 hex chars. text, not
-- uuid, because the gateway format is 'bill_...'.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.gateway_bills (
  id             text primary key
                   default 'bill_' || replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', '')
                   check (id ~ '^bill_[0-9a-f]{32}$'),
  org_id         uuid not null,
  lease_id       uuid not null,
  amount_sen     bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  status         text not null default 'pending'
                   check (status in ('pending', 'paid', 'failed')),
  transaction_id text,
  paid_at        timestamptz,
  created_by     uuid,
  created_at     timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at     timestamptz not null default now(),
  check (status <> 'paid' or paid_at is not null),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases (id, org_id)
);
create index gateway_bills_lease_id_org_id_idx on public.gateway_bills (lease_id, org_id);
create index gateway_bills_org_id_idx on public.gateway_bills (org_id);
alter table public.gateway_bills enable row level security;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- payments: append-only money received. Never deleted; status only moves
-- forward (see integrity_triggers.sql).
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.payments (
  id              uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id          uuid not null,
  lease_id        uuid not null,
  amount_sen      bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  -- Part of an online payment left over once every invoice is fully paid.
  unapplied_sen   bigint not null default 0
                    check (unapplied_sen >= 0 and unapplied_sen <= amount_sen),
  method          text not null check (method in ('cash', 'bank_transfer', 'online')),
  status          text not null
                    check (status in ('pending_verification', 'approved', 'rejected', 'voided')),
  received_at     timestamptz not null,
  -- Storage object name in bucket payment-slips: '<org_id>/...'. unique: one
  -- uploaded slip can back one payment only.
  slip_path       text unique,
  -- unique: a gateway bill creates at most one payment, ever. This is the
  -- guarantee behind webhook idempotency — a duplicate or concurrent delivery
  -- that gets past the app's checks still dies here with 23505.
  gateway_bill_id text unique references public.gateway_bills (id),
  recorded_by     uuid,
  decided_by      uuid,
  decided_at      timestamptz,
  decision_reason text,
  created_at      timestamptz not null default now(),
  constraint payments_slip_iff_bank_transfer
    check ((method = 'bank_transfer') = (slip_path is not null)),
  constraint payments_bill_iff_online
    check ((method = 'online') = (gateway_bill_id is not null)),
  -- Manual payments are capped at the remaining balance, so only an online
  -- payment can have money left over.
  constraint payments_unapplied_only_online
    check (method = 'online' or unapplied_sen = 0),
  constraint payments_reason_required
    check (status not in ('rejected', 'voided')
           or char_length(btrim(coalesce(decision_reason, ''))) >= 5),
  constraint payments_slip_in_own_org_folder
    check (slip_path is null or starts_with(slip_path, org_id::text || '/')),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases (id, org_id),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index payments_lease_id_org_id_idx on public.payments (lease_id, org_id);
create index payments_org_id_status_received_at_idx
  on public.payments (org_id, status, received_at);  -- collections report
alter table public.payments enable row level security;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- payment_allocations: how much of a payment went to which invoice.
-- invoice paid = sum(amount_sen) over its allocations.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.payment_allocations (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id     uuid not null,
  payment_id uuid not null,
  invoice_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (payment_id, invoice_id),
  foreign key (payment_id, org_id) references public.payments (id, org_id),
  foreign key (invoice_id, org_id) references public.invoices (id, org_id)
);
create index payment_allocations_invoice_id_org_id_idx
  on public.payment_allocations (invoice_id, org_id);
create index payment_allocations_payment_id_org_id_idx
  on public.payment_allocations (payment_id, org_id);
create index payment_allocations_org_id_idx on public.payment_allocations (org_id);
alter table public.payment_allocations enable row level security;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- audit_log: append-only (enforced by triggers for every role, owner included).
-- actor_id has no FK on purpose: an audit row must outlive the user, and an
-- "on delete set null" would be an UPDATE, which the log refuses.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.audit_log (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id     uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  actor_id   uuid,
  action     text not null check (char_length(btrim(action)) > 0),
  entity_id  uuid,
  details    jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb check (jsonb_typeof(details) = 'object'),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index audit_log_org_id_created_at_idx on public.audit_log (org_id, created_at desc);
create index audit_log_entity_id_idx on public.audit_log (entity_id);
alter table public.audit_log enable row level security;
-- =============================================================================
-- 3/4 Access control for the Supabase Data API (PostgREST called with the
-- publishable key + a user's token). Two layers:
--   1. GRANTs decide which operations a role may attempt at all.
--      anon: nothing. authenticated: SELECT on the brief's tables, plus
--      UPDATE of the single column tenants.phone. No INSERT/DELETE anywhere.
--   2. RLS policies decide which rows. Every policy is `to authenticated`.
-- The app's own server code uses Prisma as the owner (bypasses RLS) and does its
-- own authorization; this migration is what protects direct Data API calls.
-- =============================================================================

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Grants. Revoke whatever Supabase's default privileges handed out when the
-- tables were created, then grant back the minimum.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
revoke all on all tables    in schema public from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on all sequences in schema public from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on all functions in schema public from public, anon, authenticated;
-- The secret key (service_role) is for server-side Storage cleanup and Auth
-- admin only; it never writes tables (Prisma does), so it cannot either.
revoke insert, update, delete, truncate, references, trigger
  on all tables in schema public from service_role;

grant select on
  public.organizations,
  public.memberships,
  public.units,
  public.tenants,
  public.leases,
  public.invoices,
  public.payments,
  public.payment_allocations,
  public.gateway_bills,
  public.audit_log
to authenticated;

-- Column-level grant: "tenant updates only phone". Even with a permissive row
-- policy, UPDATE of any other column is "permission denied".
grant update (phone) on public.tenants to authenticated;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- RLS helpers. security definer so they can read memberships/tenants/leases
-- without recursing through those tables' own policies; stable so the planner
-- can evaluate `(select private.fn())` once per statement (initPlan) instead of
-- once per row. They only ever answer about auth.uid(), the caller.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
grant usage on schema private to authenticated;

-- Org of the caller as staff/manager (null if they are not a member).
create function private.member_org_id()
returns uuid
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select m.org_id from public.memberships m where m.user_id = (select auth.uid())
$$;

-- Org of the caller as manager (null if not a manager).
create function private.manager_org_id()
returns uuid
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select m.org_id from public.memberships m
  where m.user_id = (select auth.uid()) and m.role = 'manager'
$$;

-- Org of the caller as tenant (null if they have no tenant row).
create function private.tenant_org_id()
returns uuid
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select t.org_id from public.tenants t where t.user_id = (select auth.uid())
$$;

-- Leases on which the caller is the tenant.
create function private.tenant_lease_ids()
returns setof uuid
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select l.id from public.leases l
  join public.tenants t on t.id = l.tenant_id
  where t.user_id = (select auth.uid())
$$;

-- Units of the leases on which the caller is the tenant.
create function private.tenant_unit_ids()
returns setof uuid
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select l.unit_id from public.leases l
  join public.tenants t on t.id = l.tenant_id
  where t.user_id = (select auth.uid())
$$;

-- Payments on the leases on which the caller is the tenant.
create function private.tenant_payment_ids()
returns setof uuid
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select p.id from public.payments p
  join public.leases l on l.id = p.lease_id
  join public.tenants t on t.id = l.tenant_id
  where t.user_id = (select auth.uid())
$$;

revoke all on all functions in schema private from public, anon;
grant execute on function
  private.member_org_id(),
  private.manager_org_id(),
  private.tenant_org_id(),
  private.tenant_lease_ids(),
  private.tenant_unit_ids(),
  private.tenant_payment_ids()
to authenticated;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Policies. "member" = staff or manager of the row's organization.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- organizations: own organization (as member or as tenant).
create policy organizations_select on public.organizations
  for select to authenticated
  using (id = (select private.member_org_id()) or id = (select private.tenant_org_id()));

-- memberships: members of the same organization. Tenants: none.
create policy memberships_select on public.memberships
  for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = (select private.member_org_id()));

-- units: members see the organization's units; tenants the units of own leases.
create policy units_select on public.units
  for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = (select private.member_org_id())
         or id in (select private.tenant_unit_ids()));

-- tenants: members see the organization's tenants; a tenant sees own row.
create policy tenants_select on public.tenants
  for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = (select private.member_org_id())
         or user_id = (select auth.uid()));

-- A tenant may update own row; the column grant above limits it to phone.
create policy tenants_update_own_phone on public.tenants
  for update to authenticated
  using (user_id = (select auth.uid()))
  with check (user_id = (select auth.uid()));

-- leases, invoices, payments, gateway_bills: members see the organization's
-- rows; a tenant sees the rows of own leases.
create policy leases_select on public.leases
  for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = (select private.member_org_id())
         or id in (select private.tenant_lease_ids()));

create policy invoices_select on public.invoices
  for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = (select private.member_org_id())
         or lease_id in (select private.tenant_lease_ids()));

create policy payments_select on public.payments
  for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = (select private.member_org_id())
         or lease_id in (select private.tenant_lease_ids()));

create policy gateway_bills_select on public.gateway_bills
  for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = (select private.member_org_id())
         or lease_id in (select private.tenant_lease_ids()));

-- payment_allocations: members see the organization's; a tenant sees the
-- allocations of payments on own leases.
create policy payment_allocations_select on public.payment_allocations
  for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = (select private.member_org_id())
         or payment_id in (select private.tenant_payment_ids()));

-- audit_log: managers of the organization only.
create policy audit_log_select on public.audit_log
  for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = (select private.manager_org_id()));
-- =============================================================================
-- 4/4 Storage: the private payment-slips bucket, its policies, and the rule
-- "a payment's slip_path must point to an existing file in its own
-- organization's folder".
-- =============================================================================

-- Private bucket (no public URLs): reads go through short-lived signed URLs.
-- Size and type limits are enforced by Storage itself, on top of the app's check.
insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
values (
  'payment-slips',
  'payment-slips',
  false,
  5242880, -- 5 MB
  array['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'application/pdf']
)
on conflict (id) do nothing;

-- Object names are '<org_id>/<anything>'. Staff and managers may upload into,
-- and read/list, their own organization's folder only. Tenants and anon have no
-- policy, so they get nothing. There are deliberately no UPDATE/DELETE policies:
-- slips are not overwritten by users, and cleanup after a failed recording is
-- done server-side with the secret key.
create policy payment_slips_insert_own_org on storage.objects
  for insert to authenticated
  with check (
    bucket_id = 'payment-slips'
    and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select private.member_org_id())::text
  );

create policy payment_slips_select_own_org on storage.objects
  for select to authenticated
  using (
    bucket_id = 'payment-slips'
    and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select private.member_org_id())::text
  );

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- payments.slip_path must name an object that really exists in payment-slips,
-- inside the payment's own organization's folder (the CHECK on payments already
-- requires the '<org_id>/' prefix; this adds "and the file exists").
-- security definer: storage.objects is not ours to grant on, the function owner
-- (postgres) can read it.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create function private.payments_slip_exists()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if split_part(new.slip_path, '/', 1) <> new.org_id::text then
    raise exception 'slip_path must be in the organization''s own folder' using errcode = '23514';
  end if;
  if not exists (
    select 1 from storage.objects o
    where o.bucket_id = 'payment-slips' and o.name = new.slip_path
  ) then
    raise exception 'slip_path % does not exist in bucket payment-slips', new.slip_path
      using errcode = '23503';
  end if;
  return new;
end;
$$;

revoke all on function private.payments_slip_exists() from public, anon, authenticated;

create trigger payments_slip_exists
  before insert on public.payments
  for each row
  when (new.slip_path is not null)
  execute function private.payments_slip_exists();

## Access-control tests: 70/70 passing, no bugs found in src

`pnpm vitest run tests/access.test.ts tests/data-api.test.ts` passes: 2 files, 70 tests (42 access + 28 data-api), about 40 s. `pnpm typecheck` is clean across the repo. eslint and prettier are clean on my three files. Nothing committed, and src/** untouched.

Two runs failed mid-way because another agent ran `db reset` ("Connection terminated", "table does not exist"). Rerunning fixed it each time.

**Files (all mine, new):**
- `C:\Users\Lenovo\Desktop\ezyfusion-rent-collection\tests\helpers\auth-users.ts`: `buildWorld()` creates real Auth users through the admin API with unique `t-<label>-<tag>@example.test` emails. It does not depend on the seed. It adds memberships and tenant rows through Prisma, then builds org A (manager, staff, tenant A1 with lease L1 plus a lease starting in 2030, tenant A2 with L2) and org B (manager, tenant B1 with LB). It also adds a user whose `user_metadata` says "manager of org A" but who has no membership. Leases, payments (L1: one approved, one pending; LB: one approved) and gateway bills all go through the services. Sign-in is by password; if the local Auth limit of 30 sign-ins per 5 minutes is hit, it falls back to a magic-link token (a real session). A run uses about 15 sign-ins.
- `C:\Users\Lenovo\Desktop\ezyfusion-rent-collection\tests\access.test.ts`: calls the route handlers directly with real Bearer tokens. Every refusal checks the status, that the body is exactly `{ error: string }`, and that a full snapshot of both orgs (leases, invoices, payments, allocations, bills, audit count, tenants, memberships) is unchanged. `next/headers` is mocked to an empty cookie jar so the "no header" case tests the cookie fallback.
- `C:\Users\Lenovo\Desktop\ezyfusion-rent-collection\tests\data-api.test.ts`: supabase-js with the publishable key, as anon and as each user. The expected rows are computed with Prisma from the brief's table, so read checks compare exact sets.

**What access.test.ts covers:**
- **401:** 10 kinds of bad login on all 8 endpoints:
  - no header, garbage token, empty Bearer, wrong scheme, token with no scheme, two tokens
  - a real token with a rewritten payload, an `alg:none` token, a signed-out session
  - the metadata-only "manager"

  Also: 401 comes before 404, and a user token does not get past the webhook's signature check.
- **GET lease:** the brief's exact response shape:
  - invoices in allocation order, compared against `generateSchedule`
  - deposit allocated first
  - `receivedAt` is ISO with an offset and is the same instant
  - staff and tenant get the same body as the manager

  404 for: the other tenant, org B, a non-UUID, an unknown id, a payment id.
- **POST leases:**
  - 201 in the manager's own org; an `orgId` in the body is ignored; invoice count matches the schedule; audit row written.
  - 403 for staff and tenants, even with an invalid body.
  - 404 for another org's unit or tenant (and manager B using org A's), with nothing created.
  - 409 for overlap with both ends inclusive; the next day after a lease ends gets 201.
  - 15 invalid bodies get 400.
- **POST payments:**
  - staff gets pending, manager gets approved; ids and status in the body are ignored.
  - 403 for the lease's own tenant, 404 for the other tenant or org B.
  - 422 at the cap + 1.
  - 20 invalid bodies get 400: no offset, future date, slip on a cash payment, missing slip, slip in another org's folder, slip that doesn't exist, `../` traversal, slip reused.
- **Approve, reject, void:** 403 and 404 for the right roles; reason shorter than 5 characters (after trimming) gets 400; the 409 state transitions; voiding removes the allocations.
- **Gateway bills:** 201 with the due-today (Malaysia time) amount and a `bill_` + 32-hex id; 422 when nothing is due; 403 for staff and manager; 404 for others.
- **Collections report:**
  - one entry per month; 00:30 Malaysia time on 1 March counts in March; pending payments excluded; each org sees only its own; year boundary.
  - 403 for tenants before input is checked; 11 bad ranges get 400.
- **Extra:** `GET /slips/:paymentId` (302 with no-store for staff and manager, 401/403/404 for the rest).

**What data-api.test.ts covers:**
- **Reads:** exact visible-row sets per role.
  - Anon sees nothing.
  - Tenant A1 sees two leases and only those leases' children; no memberships or audit_log.
  - Filtering by id or embedding related tables doesn't get past RLS.
  - Staff sees no audit_log; managers see only their own org's audit_log; the metadata-only user sees nothing.
- **Phone column:** a tenant can update their own phone. Other columns fail with a permission error (Postgres code 42501). Other users' updates change 0 rows, and an unfiltered update only touches the caller's own row. A badly formatted phone is rejected by the CHECK constraint.
- **Writes:** for anon, tenant, staff, manager A, manager B and the service role, insert, update and delete on all 10 tables each fail with 42501 (a permission refusal, not some unrelated error), and the database is unchanged.
- **RPC:** fails through both the public and private schemas.
- **Catalog checks** (these would also catch tables added later):
  - RLS is enabled on every table.
  - anon has no privilege on anything in `public`.
  - No function can be executed by anon or authenticated.
  - The only column-level write grant is `authenticated UPDATE tenants.phone`; the service role has no write grants.
- **Storage:**
  - The bucket is private, and its public URL fails.
  - Staff A can upload, sign, fetch and list in org A's folder. Uploads to org B's folder or the bucket root fail, and so do wrong file types, overwrites and deletes.
  - Tenants, org B, the metadata-only user and anon cannot upload, download, sign or list.

**Real bugs in src:** none found.

**Ambiguities and what I could not test:**
- A malformed `unitId`/`tenantId` in POST /api/leases returns 404 (`src/lib/server/services/leases.ts`, the `isUuid` check before the transaction). The brief could also be read as 400, so the test accepts either and checks nothing was created.
- A user with no membership and no tenant row gets 401 (`getActor` returns null). That matches "no valid login" but is a judgement call; the test asserts 401.
- The cookie session path is only tested as "no cookie means 401"; a real browser cookie session is not exercised.
- A user who has both a membership and a tenant row: on the API the membership wins, but the database's RLS shows them the union of both. The brief doesn't cover it, so it isn't tested.
- Concurrency is left to the payments and webhook tests.
- Each run leaves its test orgs and auth users in the database, as the existing fixtures do.
